item.title: Wizard output equals the equivalent answers fixture
item.text:
{"record":{"id":"REQ-RUN-0603","title":"Wizard output equals the equivalent answers fixture","status":"Active","version":"1.0.0","created":"2026-09-19","last_updated":"2026-09-20","owner":"randlee","supersedes":null,"superseded_by":null,"requirement_statement":{"text":"Equal means the two parsed JSON values are equal: the same keys, each with the same value and JSON type. Key order and whitespace do not matter.

The generated-tree comparison is an automated test. The test stubs Wyvern, so
CI does not need the real binary. It runs the driver once with that stub
returning the answers in one fixture, and once with `--var-file` on the same
fixture, then compares the two generated trees. The comparison excludes
`target/`, the `[patch.crates-io]` checkout patch (the generated root `Cargo.toml` section mapping SDK crate names to local checkout paths), `.sc-lint/venv/` (the
local sc-lint install embeds the destination path), and `.sc-compose/logs/`
(the generator log contains timestamps). Success criteria 1 to 3 remain the
check that a machine with Wyvern emits that fixture.","statements":[{"modal":"Must","text":"The answers JSON object produced by the Wyvern wizard under `wizard/` MUST validate against `wizard/answers.schema.json`."},{"modal":"Must","text":"When a person makes the same choices in the wizard as an answers fixture in `wizard/fixtures/` contains, the parsed JSON answers object produced by the wizard MUST equal the parsed JSON fixture: both have the same keys, and each corresponding value is equal with the same JSON type. Object key order and whitespace do not affect equality."},{"modal":"Must","text":"A project generated from the wizard's answers MUST have the same file paths and byte-for-byte file contents as the project generated from the equal fixture with `--var-file`, excluding `target/`, the `[patch.crates-io]` checkout patch, `.sc-lint/venv/`, and `.sc-compose/logs/` from the generated-tree comparison."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"The wizard MUST NOT emit a key that the schema does not define."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"It MUST NOT omit a key that the schema requires."}]},"rationale":"Because the wizard and a hand-written answers file produce the same JSON,
nothing else in the system depends on which one was used. That is what lets
the wizard be built last, slip, or be reshaped without touching the schema,
the template, the driver or CI.","success_criteria":{"text":"1. On a machine with Wyvern installed, run the wizard and choose the project
   name, `db = sqlite`, `mcp = true` and the licence exactly as
   `wizard/fixtures/sqlite-mcp.json` has them. Save the resulting answers
   object to `out.json`.
2. `out.json` validates against `wizard/answers.schema.json`.
3. A comparison of the parsed JSON of `out.json` and
   `wizard/fixtures/sqlite-mcp.json` reports them equal (for example
   `python3 -c "import json,sys; sys.exit(json.load(open('out.json')) !=
   json.load(open('wizard/fixtures/sqlite-mcp.json')))"` exits 0).
4. Generate one project from `out.json` and one from the fixture, both with
   `--var-file`, into two directories. `diff -r` of the two directories,
   ignoring build output, reports no difference.
5. An automated test stubs Wyvern, runs the driver once from that stub with
   the answers in `wizard/fixtures/sqlite-mcp.json` and once with
   `--var-file` on that fixture, and compares the generated trees. Paths
   under `target/`, `.sc-lint/venv/`, and `.sc-compose/logs/` are ignored.
   The `[patch.crates-io]` checkout patch is ignored. Every other file
   matches.","acceptance_criteria":[],"test_evidence":[]},"dependencies":{"text":"","requires":[],"related":[]},"product_applicability":{"text":"","applies_to":[],"does_not_apply_to":[]},"implementation_notes":{"text":"","key_considerations":[]},"test_strategy":{"text":"","test_types":[]},"related_documents":{"text":"","requirements":[],"architecture_decisions":[],"design_documents":[],"work_items":[],"external_references":[]}},"target_statement_indices":[2,3]}

item.title: Standard crates, used the documented way
item.text:
{"record":{"id":"NFR-RUN-0003","title":"Standard crates, used the documented way","status":"Active","version":"1.0.0","created":"2026-09-19","last_updated":"2026-11-12","owner":"randlee","supersedes":null,"superseded_by":null,"requirement_statement":{"text":"Definitions: CLI means command-line interface. MCP means Model Context Protocol. HTTP means Hypertext Transfer Protocol. SQL means Structured Query Language. API means application programming interface. ADR means architecture decision record. A building block is a crate used to provide one of the jobs listed in the Job/Crate table. A documented API is an API shown in that crate's documentation for the selected job. A governing requirement or explicit amendment takes precedence over the table's crate choice for a job it specifically addresses.

No command path must be hand-written. A later consumer-side generator may produce that path against the delivered sc-runtime. The existing repo-internal macro policy and its success criteria stand; Phase D builds no generator. The historical generator clause below does not forbid consumer-side command generation.

The prohibited list below was a design recommendation, not an owner requirement, and three of its entries no longer bind as written. (1) "A command or operation registry" does not forbid the shared command path of PRD §3. (2) "A portable query layer" forbids passing SQL across backends; it does not forbid `Storage<T>`, which carries no SQL and is required by PRD-STO-2. (3) "A macro system" and "a code generator of its own" are undecided, not prohibited: the owner is considering an sc-compose or syn-based generator (PRD §9). Success criterion 1 stands until that decision. The prohibition on wrapper types around `axum`, `rmcp` and `sqlx` stands.

The Job/Crate table lists the chosen crates:

| Job | Crate |
|---|---|
| HTTP server and router | `axum` 0.8 |
| MCP server | `rmcp` 3.x (`StreamableHttpService`, `#[tool]`, `#[tool_router]`) |
| OpenAPI | `utoipa` and `utoipa-axum` (`OpenApiRouter`, `routes!`) |
| SQL | `sqlx` 0.9 |
| CLI parsing | `clap` derive |
| HTTP client | `reqwest` 0.13 |
| template rendering | `cargo-generate` |

- a command or operation registry;
- a macro system of its own: no crate with `proc-macro = true`, and no
  `macro_rules!` macro that defines operations, routes or tools;
- a code generator of its own, including a generated Rust HTTP client;
- a portable query layer, meaning any abstraction that lets one query run on
  more than one database backend;
- a wrapper type around an `axum`, `rmcp` or `sqlx` type in a public API. The
  project passes `sc_runtime::Daemon::builder()` an ordinary
  `utoipa_axum::OpenApiRouter` and an ordinary `rmcp` service.","statements":[{"modal":"Must","text":"For each job in the Job/Crate table, `crates/` and `template/` MUST reuse the listed crate's capability through its documented API, except where a governing requirement or explicit amendment specifies another implementation."},{"modal":"MustNot","text":"The repository MUST NOT contain, in `crates/` or in `template/`, the items in the prohibited list in this record’s Requirement Statement, subject to the amendments stated there."}]},"rationale":"Each item in the prohibited list would be code this project has to maintain
and every generated project has to learn, where a standard crate already does
the job and is already documented. Standard designs are preferred over
hand-rolled pieces throughout. The decision that standard designs are
preferred, and that this item and [NFR-RUN-0004](requirements.md) enforce it,
is recorded in [ADR-RUN-0008](architecture.md).","success_criteria":{"text":"1. `grep -rn "proc-macro" --include=Cargo.toml crates template` prints
   nothing.
2. The `arch-qa` architecture review checks the public API of each of the
   four crates against [ADR-RUN-0001](architecture.md), which states that the
   framework builds the parts and the project wires them in ordinary Rust. It
   reports no registry type, no generator and no public newtype or trait
   whose only purpose is to hide an `axum`, `rmcp` or `sqlx` type.
3. Inspection of the template: the example routes are registered with
   `utoipa_axum::routes!` on an `OpenApiRouter`, the example MCP tools use
   `#[tool]` and `#[tool_router]`, and the CLI uses `clap` derive.
4. `grep -rn "macro_rules!" crates/*/src template` prints nothing, or every
   match is reviewed and found not to define operations, routes or tools.","acceptance_criteria":[],"test_evidence":[]},"dependencies":{"text":"","requires":[],"related":[]},"product_applicability":{"text":"","applies_to":[],"does_not_apply_to":[]},"implementation_notes":{"text":"","key_considerations":[]},"test_strategy":{"text":"","test_types":[]},"related_documents":{"text":"","requirements":[],"architecture_decisions":[],"design_documents":[],"work_items":[],"external_references":[]}},"target_statement_indices":[1,2]}
